title: Passage and Landfall
premise: Rosalind Sterling, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Meridian Optimists—a salvage syndicate that calls its violence 'investment'—is given a dying prospector's map to the wreck of the Corvane, a treasure ship lost in the Sable Archipelago, in exchange for a promise to deliver his letters home. Racing the monsoon and the Optimists' fleet, she gathers an unlikely crew: her estranged half-brother, a disgraced tide-pilot, and the prospector's granddaughter who arrives demanding answers. Betrayal, mutiny, and six tides of impossible weather later, Rosalind reaches the wreck first, but chooses to split the find—paying her debt, honoring the promise, and discovering that the family she built on the water was the true inheritance.
about_author: Odile Ravensworth is a former maritime surveyor who spent seven years charting cyclone corridors across the Coral Sea before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels from a converted pilot boat moored off Queensland, where she keeps a barometer that has never once been wrong.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Smile
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the port city of Vantrell, Rosalind loses her chase plane to creditors and learns the Meridian Optimists have bought her debt—and expect repayment within a season. A dying prospector, Elias Wren, witnesses her humiliation and offers her a map to the Corvane in exchange for one promise. Beat: desperation meets opportunity.

chapters.title: A Promise Worth Dying On
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Elias dies before dawn, leaving Rosalind the map, a sealed bundle of letters, and a warning about the sixth tide. She studies the route through the Sable Archipelago and realizes the monsoon will close the passage in weeks—the same window the Optimists' fleet needs. Beat: reluctant commitment hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Crew of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rosalind and Juniper Wren. Rosalind recruits the disgraced tide-pilot Sefa and discovers her estranged half-brother Callum working the docks; meanwhile Elias's granddaughter Juniper tracks Rosalind down, furious, demanding her grandfather's letters. Beat: friction, accusation, and the grudging start of found family.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The crew sails on the patched ketch Vespera as Sefa calculates their race against the fleet: they must reach the wreck by the sixth tide before landfall or lose the passage entirely. First Optimist scout ship sighted astern. Beat: the clock starts ticking; camaraderie forms under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Letters Said
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Juniper finally reads Elias's letters and learns he abandoned her mother for this obsession—and that the map is partly a confession. She confronts Rosalind mid-storm-scout, and their argument nearly wrecks the Vespera on an uncharted reef. Beat: grief and anger forcing honesty.

chapters.title: The Optimists' Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Callum. The Optimists' flagship overtakes them; their captain offers Callum the map's coordinates in exchange for betraying Rosalind and clearing his own debts. Callum wavers, copies the chart, but returns without handing it over—though the fleet now knows their heading. Beat: temptation survived, trust tested.

chapters.title: Mutiny at the Third Reef
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A crew member Rosalind hired in Vantrell is revealed as an Optimist plant and tries to seize the Vespera at the treacherous Third Reef. In the fight the ship takes damage and Sefa is injured; Juniper's knowledge of Elias's notes saves them through the reef. Beat: betrayal paid for, loyalty proven.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV alternating all four. The monsoon makes landfall early; the fifth tide comes black and screaming. The Vespera limps into the wreck lagoon hours ahead of the Optimist fleet, which is scattered by the storm. On the seabed below, the Corvane's masts glint through clearing water. Beat: triumph shadowed by exhaustion and dread.

chapters.title: The Weight of Gold
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Diving the wreck, Rosalind finds not just treasure but Elias's own log from decades ago—he'd found it once before and turned back, choosing his granddaughter over the gold. The Optimists' surviving ship arrives armed. Rosalind must decide what the inheritance is actually worth. Beat: climax of values; the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Using the monsoon itself as cover, the crew fakes the Vespera's destruction, hides the recovered cargo with islanders who owed Elias a debt, and lets the Optimists salvage an empty hull. Debts settled, letters delivered, the found family sails north together. Beat: resolution—memory honored, inheritance redefined.
